description: We are a team of students passionate about space, technology, creativity, and learning. We aim to build an interesting and meaningful project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge while gaining new skills and having fun. We welcome teammates interested in research, storytelling, coding, design, presentation, or creative ideas. No advanced experience is required—enthusiasm and teamwork matter most! 🚀🌕
summary: Forgotten Missions is an interactive digital space museum that brings the stories of NASA hardware left on the Moon and Mars to life. Visitors can explore six student-friendly stories—from the Apollo 11 lunar module descent stage and laser retroreflector to Perseverance’s parachute, backshell and sky-crane descent stage. Each story explains what the equipment did, why it remained, and how it contributed to exploration or science. The prototype organizes stories by world, connects facts to NASA source records, and makes mission history easier for young space enthusiasts to discover. Its goal is to turn objects often described as debris into understandable records of engineering, exploration and scientific legacy.
details: Forgotten Missions is an interactive digital space museum that documents human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars during space exploration. The website presents six stories covering objects such as the Apollo 11 lunar module descent stage, lunar laser retroreflector, ALSEP equipment, Surveyor 3, and components of the Perseverance rover's landing system. Users can explore the objects through an interactive website, discover their original purpose, understand why they remained, and learn about their contribution to exploration and science. The website includes Moon and Mars filters, expandable story panels, and links to NASA references. We developed the prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with GitHub Pages for public hosting. ChatGPT assisted with brainstorming, drafting, and initial code generation. Our goal is to make space exploration history accessible and engaging, while showing that equipment left behind can still have scientific, historical, and engineering value.
